newsitem.title: INDIA: Flood-hit Gujarat evacuates over 57,000 people.
newsitem.headline: Flood-hit Gujarat evacuates over 57,000 people.

text.p: More than 57,000 people marooned by floods that killed at least 168 people in India's western state of Gujarat were moved to safety over the weekend, state officials and local news agencies reported on Monday.

Police and soldiers used boats to move more than 57,000 people to higher ground after their homes were swamped by the rising waters of the Kharicut canal in the industrial city of Ahmedabad, the Press Trust of India (PTI) said.
"The army and state reserve police personnel were engaged in rescuing people from the marooned areas," it added.
The canal waters blocked a national highway.

PTI said that at least 168 people had died during the week-long rains that have flooded many parts of the usually drought-prone state. Many drowned, or died in house collapses, or were swept away by fast-flowing rivers.
The news agency said district authorities distributed relief packages as well as small sums of cash to the flood-affected. Many people were temporarily housed in nearby local schools.
A large number of non-governmental groups were also distributing food and blankets, officials said.
The water flooded six villages on the outskirts of Ahmedabad, and levels were rising in six more, they added.
"Relief operations have been taken up on a war-footing," Gujarat Chief Minister Shankersinh Vaghela told reporters in Ahmedabad, after an aerial survey of the flood-hit areas.
But the fury of the rains had subsided, and the flood waters were beginning to recede, he added.
Vaghela estimated the damage to roads and property at 5.5 billion rupees ($153.8 million), PTI said. Relief and rescue operations would cost an estimated 510 million rupees, he added.
Oilseed traders said the floods had delayed groundnut sowing in Gujarat, which produces about 35 percent of India's total groundnut output, by at least 10 days. Sowing usually starts by end-June.
"There is heavy water-logging in the fields in Gujarat," said Navinbhai Shah, president of the Bombay Oilseeds and Oil Exchange Ltd. "Sowing would now be possible only in the second week of July."
